text:
The passing of Rene Clert Baterbonia is not only a heartbreaking loss for Ateneo but for Philippine basketball as a whole. We were deprived of witnessing the full extent of his greatness. With his talent, dedication, and potential, he could have proudly represented the country in Gilas Pilipinas, built a successful career in the PBA, and perhaps even competed in international leagues. His dreams were cut tragically short, but his legacy and the lives he touched will never be forgotten.

Our deepest and most sincere condolences to Rene’s family, loved ones, teammates, coaches, and the entire Ateneo community. May you find strength and comfort during this incredibly difficult time. Rest in peace, Rene. 🕊️🏀

text:
I find it so wrong that this priest and President of the university seemingly used the initial grieving stage of the parents as his excuse for not coming out and speaking up and explaining right away.  THINGS LIKE THAT have to be done immediately. THERE SHOULD HAVE BEEN A SENSE OF URGENCY. That is actually an indicator of how devastated and remorseful you are in such a situation. Instead, the much delayed reaction and apparently carefully curated statements of the  university officials and coaches showed indifference, lack of empathy, lack of sincerity. This statement by this priest and President of the university only  worsens the curent perception that the priests and officials of ADMU are more concerned about the reputation and public perception of the university. 

C'mon ADMU, "people in the know" are aware of other things that have happened in the recent past (and prior) that involved other student-athletes which ADMU kept mum about and "sort of swept under the rug" so that non-Ateneans wouldn't become aware of them, thus, preserving the "highly respected and immaculate historical reputation" of ADMU. Yes, FYI, Mister ADMU President, there are non-Ateneans (not too many though) who are aware of those things.     NO RECOGITION OR AWARD OR HONOR OR HISTORICAL REPUTATION OR EVEN A SPORTS CHAMPIONSHIP IS WORTH MORE THAN THE LIVES OF THOSE TWO STUDENT ATHLETES THAT WERE LOST ON THAT FATEFUL DAY. 

And I hope that, as a sign of remorse and respect for Rene and Divine and their families, ADMU WILL (aside from penalizing the basketball team officials involved) VOLUNTARILY take a leave of absence from this next UAAP men's basketball tournament. Let that serve as your "One Minute Of Silence" to remember the lives of those two student-athletes whose lives were lost in that tragic incident. It will also show the world that ATENEO VALUES the (lost) lives and the future of their student-athletes MORE THAN winning a sports championship!

Lastly, I hope that the officials and coaches of the other UAAP schools as well as the member schools of the NCAA will learn valuable lessons from this tragedy and will incorporate those lessons into their different sports programs to ensure that the lives (and future) of their own student-athletes are not put in danger and risked so much just to increase their team's competitiveness and chances of winning. There are physical limitations. MORE SO, THERE IS A RIGHT WAY to do things to reach one's full potential as an athlete. That would be the best way to somehow give some meaning to the demise of Rene and Divine.

text:
Sa kulturang Pilipino, ang lamay at pakikiramay ay hindi lang basta tradisyon—ito ay isang panlipunang obligasyon at institusyon ng kolektibong pagdadalamhati.

Ang Kultura ng "Lamay" vs. Korporadang Katahimikan
Pakikipagkapwa sa Oras ng Sawi: Sa Pilipinas, kapag may namatayan, binubuksan ang pinto ng bahay o kapilya para sa lahat. Ang pagpunta ng mga kaibigan, kakilala, o maging ng mga pinuno ng komunidad ay simbolo ng pag-akay sa bigat ng dusa. Ang "pribadong pagdadalamhati" o private grieving ay madalas na nakikita sa kulturang Kanluranin, ngunit sa kontekstong Pilipino, ang pagtatago o hindi pagsipot ay pwedeng makahulugan bilang pagwawalang-bahala, kawalan ng utang na loob, o pag-iwas sa pananagutan.

Ang Pagliban sa Pamilya Baterbonia: Kaya naman napakabigat ng mantsa na hindi sila sumipot sa pamilya Baterbonia. Sa pananaw ng ordinaryong Pilipino, hindi sapat na "binayaran ang funeral expenses at pamasahe". Ang pagpapadala ng pera nang walang pisikal na pagharap at pakikiramay ay nagmumukhang transaksyonal—parang binabayaran ang katahimikan o tinatapos ang obligasyon sa pamamagitan ng tseke, imbis na puso at pakikipagkapwa.

I don’t believe this is about revenge. I believe people are asking for justice and accountability. My heart breaks for these young lives and for the families who are now left to carry this unimaginable loss. While the drowning was unfortunate, that does not mean it was unavoidable and unforeseeable. When there is negligence, risk and danger that could’ve been prevented, and a failure to act despite previous near-drowning incidents, accountability matters.
It’s no different from a fatal drunk-driving accident. You know the risks, yet you choose to proceed anyway, and lives are lost as a result. An incident may be unintended, but negligence can still make people responsible for its consequences. Those who planned, approved, and conducted these activities should answer for their decisions. Two precious lives were lost, and with them, the dreams, hopes, and futures they carried. Their families have suffered a loss that can never truly be repaired. Seeking accountability is not revenge. It is the minimum owed to the victims, their loved ones, and to everyone who deserves assurance that such a tragedy will never happen again.
